subject: MedoSys pilot — evaluation playbook, acceptance checklist, and cutover cadence
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@medosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: MedoSys evaluation playbook and acceptance checklist

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a concise evaluation playbook so we can shorten the pilot and have a predictable close. Attached: MedoSys_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones) and a short privacy Q&A.

High level (proposed):
- Duration: 3 weeks (verification sprint + ramp + signoff)
- Success criteria (must pass all to move to post-pilot pricing):
  • End-to-end latency P95 ≤ 450ms at expected concurrency (20 rps)
  • Inference cost per 1k tokens within target budget (you provided $X range)
  • No data exfiltration flags in privacy scans; KMS integration tested
  • Business-critical accuracy checks: F1 ≥ 0.86 on the 200-case test set
- Exit gates (hard):
  • Security review complete (SOC2 evidence + privacy qa)
  • Production API key rotation and audit logging enabled
  • Performance within SLOs for two 4-hour soak windows
- Acceptance tests (examples):
  • Latency soak: two runs of 4 hours at 20 rps (collect P50/P95/P99)
  • Regression tests: 200-case dataset with pass/fail thresholds
  • Failure-mode test: simulated node preemption — automatic fallback to variant model

Questions for you:
1) Does the list of success criteria match what your execs expect for signoff?
2) Any constraints on dates for procurement/legal review we should plan around?

Next steps:
- If you approve, we’ll lock dates in the MAP and schedule a 30-min go/no-go review at the end of week 3.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: MedoSys_MAP_v1.xlsx, privacy_qa.pdf
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@medosys.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medosys.com>, procurement@medosys.com
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: MedoSys evaluation playbook and acceptance checklist

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear plan. This looks promising and covers most of what our CTO and Head of Product asked for. A few clarifications:

- The accuracy threshold (F1 ≥ 0.86) is fine but can we add a secondary metric for precision on high-risk classes?
- Procurement needs a 10-business-day window for contract redlines. Can we schedule the go/no-go a week later than your proposed end date to accommodate?
- We'll need a short write-up of how audit logs are stored and retention window (we retain certain logs for 7 years).

I’m copying Raj (ops) and procurement to loop them in. We prefer a final signoff call on Jul 14 or 15 — either works if your team can hold it.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Senior Product Manager, MedoSys Health

Sophie —

Appreciate the quick feedback. We can add a precision threshold for the high-risk classes (precision ≥ 0.82) as a secondary metric — I’ll add that to the MAP.

Procurement window understood. Revised timeline below (attached updated MAP):
- Week 0 (prep): contract + KMS onboarding + initial test data drop (Jul 6–9)
- Week 1 (verification sprint): run regression tests, baseline model checks (Jul 10–16)
- Week 2 (soak/ramp): two soak windows and resilience tests (Jul 17–23)
- Week 3 (signoff and pricing): internal review, procurement signoff, go/no-go meeting (target Jul 14–16 but moved to Jul 24 to accommodate procurement)

Connor is looping in a short set of automated test cases (pilot_test_cases.md) and an SRE runbook stub for the soak windows. If this timeline works we’ll lock the DocuSign milestone and schedule the go/no-go on Jul 24.

Action items I’ll handle:
- Update MAP with precision metric and procurement buffer (done)
- Run initial performance baseline on your sample dataset once we receive it (need test data by Jul 10)

Marissa / Connor / Steph — FYI on the acceptance tests and runbook attached.

Thanks —
Dylan

Subject: Re: Pilot: MedoSys evaluation playbook and acceptance checklist

Sophie / team —

Quick technical notes and acceptance-test checklist from my side:

- Environment setup:
  • Provide a 10–20 GB sample payload (anonymized) for baseline passes.
  • We will provision a dedicated inference pool with pinned model version and enable KV cache.
- Performance measurements:
  • Baseline run: single instance, 1000 requests, measure P50/P95/P99 and token cost.
  • Soak run: 4 hours at 20 rps — we’ll capture traces and top-10 slow RPCs.
- Failure scenarios to validate exit gates:
  • Preempt node: simulate GPU preemption and verify automatic fallback to lower-cost variant (no user-facing errors).
  • KMS rotation: rotate a test key mid-soak and validate reconnect + no token loss.
- Acceptance test pass criteria (pass = yes/no):
  • Latency P95 ≤ 450ms across both soak windows
  • Regression F1 ≥ 0.86 AND precision (high-risk) ≥ 0.82
  • No critical privacy findings from the privacy_qa scan
  • Audit logs present for all API calls with retention metadata

I’ll run the baseline after we get the anonymized sample (deadline Jul 10 to keep the timeline). I’ve attached a short pilot_test_cases.md with exact commands and expected outputs.

—Connor
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
